prompt: A realistic still from a 1950s three-strip Technicolor film: colour impossibly saturated, everything slightly too vivid, like a memory, with a hand-painted backdrop behind real people. Camera low at the height of the firebox, fresh banknotes scattered on the stone floor in the foreground. In a hidden 1920s basement print room, a huge cast-iron printing press throws sheets of banknotes into the air. Beside it a tall skinny man in a bowler hat with a heavy gold mayoral chain round his neck, a long narrow face, hollow cheeks and a pencil-thin grey moustache, shovels coal into the press's red-hot firebox, grinning. Behind him an exhausted stoker in a soot-black vest sits slumped against the brick wall. Riveted pipes, brass gauges, steam. Key: a hard theatrical spotlight from above right. Coloured gels on the set: rich scarlet on the near surfaces, the shadows lit deep emerald. Plain margins with no writing. Thanks.
